title: Training Dataset — Instruction Pair
description: JSONL format for fine-tuning datasets. Each line is one JSON object matching this schema.
$comment: EVAL-GATE SEMANTICS (Pillar 3 SSOT — see brain/training/evaluator.py, models.py). The fine-tune is gated, before it can serve, on its quality on this dataset, but the gate is built to measure GENERALIZATION, not memorization: (1) HELD-OUT SPLIT — the worker holds out the last ~20% of rows (>=1 row; brain.training.models.split_holdout) and trains only on the rest; the gate scores ONLY the held-out rows, never rows the model trained on. (2) RESPONSE-ONLY LOSS — the score is the cross-entropy on the `response` tokens only; the `prompt`/`system` tokens are masked out (label -100), so it reflects the model's ability to produce the target answer, not to model the operator's prompt text. (3) score = exp(-avg_response_loss) = 1/perplexity, clamped to [0,1]. (4) THE GATE (brain.training.models.passes_eval_gate) — an adapter is promotable if it passes EITHER path: ABSOLUTE `score >= eval_score_threshold` (default 0.6, ~perplexity 1.67), OR IMPROVEMENT — it clears a low sanity floor (`eval_min_floor`, default 0.05) AND beats the base model on the SAME held-out split by `eval_min_improvement` (default 0.05). The base (un-adapted) model is scored on the same split and the adapter-minus-base delta is reported (base_score/score_delta). The improvement path exists because a small base model cannot reach the absolute perplexity bar even on an ideal task, yet a fine-tune that reliably out-scores its base has demonstrably learned the target behavior (§A3.2). An adapter that passes neither → EvalGateFailed (HTTP 422), not registered, endpoint cannot bind it.

prompt.description: The instruction or question given to the model.

response.description: The ideal response the model should produce.

metadata.description: Optional arbitrary metadata (source, quality score, etc.)
